title: Chatbots & Assistants
hook: ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini feel like talking to a person, but they're generative AI with a chat wrapper — brilliant writing partners, unreliable encyclopedias.
key_points: A chatbot is a generative AI you steer with plain-language conversation.
Great for drafting, summarizing, explaining, brainstorming, and rewording.
Weak as a source of facts — it can sound certain while being wrong.
Treat it as a fast, tireless assistant whose work you still check.
content_html: ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are the friendly face of generative AI: you type in plain English, and they reply in plain English. That conversational feel is genuinely new and genuinely useful — you can ask follow-up questions, request a different tone, or say "make it shorter" and it just works. Under the hood, though, it's the same next-word prediction as any generative model, dressed up as a chat. Knowing that tells you exactly where it shines and where it stumbles.
extra_html: Where it shines: anything that's really a language task. Drafting an awkward email, summarizing a long document, explaining a confusing topic three different ways, brainstorming names, turning bullet points into prose, or rewording something for a different audience. Where it stumbles: being a source of truth. Because it generates what sounds plausible, it can invent facts, citations, or quotes with total confidence. The healthiest habit is to treat a chatbot as a brilliant, tireless assistant who occasionally makes things up — lean on it for first drafts and thinking-out-loud, but verify any fact, number, or name before you rely on it.

related.title: Generative AI
related.hook: The AI behind ChatGPT and image generators doesn't look up answers — it predicts what plausibly comes next, one piece at a time, until it has built a whole response.

related.title: Talking to AI
related.hook: The difference between a useless answer and a great one is usually the question. Give the AI context, an example, and a clear job — and treat it as a conversation, not a vending machine.

related.title: When AI Makes Things Up
related.hook: AI 'hallucinations' aren't glitches — they're the technology working as designed. A model that always predicts a plausible next word will sometimes produce a plausible falsehood.

related.title: Which Chatbot Should I Use?
related.hook: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Meta AI — they're more alike than different. The honest answer to 'which is best' is: the one you'll actually open, plus a second to cross-check.

related.title: How a Language Model Works
related.hook: A chatbot isn't reading and thinking — it's running the world's most sophisticated autocomplete, picking each next word from probabilities learned across billions of sentences.

flashcards.prompt: What is a chatbot best suited for?

choices.text: Drafting, summarizing, explaining, and rewording text
Being a fully reliable source of facts

flashcards.explanation_html: Chatbots shine at language tasks — drafting and explaining — but can state wrong facts confidently, so verify anything that matters.

flashcards.prompt: What's a good mental model for using a chatbot?
flashcards.back_html: A fast, tireless assistant whose work you still review — not an oracle and not a search engine.
